backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/disputes.rs:367-384 (list_disputes) takes `_user: AuthUser` (discarded) and `Query(query): Query<ListDisputesQuery>`, then calls `state.dispute_repo.list(query.organization_id, (&query).into())` — i.e. the org id is read directly from the client query string and NEVER checked against the caller's tenant. The same pattern repeats at :387-404 (get_statistics) which calls `.get_statistics(query.organization_id)`. The in-file comment at :415 even says 'The organization is derived from the caller's JWT tenant (never a query- or body-supplied org)' — true for get_kpis via require_org(&user) at :420, but violated by list_disputes and get_statistics. The repo backing it (backend/crates/db/src/repositories/dispute.rs:120-168 `pub async fn list`) runs `.fetch_all(&self.pool)` on the raw pool — not an RlsConnection — so there is NO row-level security to catch the missing handler check (confirmed by the comment at dispute.rs:171-177 that reads 'the management API pool does not enforce RLS'). Reachable: lib.rs:333 mounts the router at `/api/v1/disputes`, and the routes are registered at disputes.rs:37 (GET /) and :38 (GET /statistics). Attack: an authenticated principal in org A issues `GET /api/v1/disputes/?organization_id=<org_B_uuid>` and receives org B's full dispute list including titles, descriptions (via ILIKE search column exposure) and party counts; same for `/statistics`. Fix shape: replace the `_user` placeholder with `user: AuthUser`, drop `organization_id` from ListDisputesQuery/OrgQuery, and derive `let org_id = require_org(&user)?;` as get_kpis already does.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/property_valuation.rs:498-545 — the three adjustment handlers (`list_adjustments`, `create_adjustment`, `delete_adjustment`) each take `_auth: AuthUser` (discarded) and act on a client-supplied `Path(comparable_id)` or `Path(adjustment_id)` with NO organization check. The backing repo calls at backend/crates/db/src/repositories/property_valuation.rs:582-628 (`create_adjustment`, `list_adjustments`) and :631-638 (`delete_adjustment`) all run `.fetch_all/.execute(&self.pool)` on the raw pool — no RLS, no org filter in the SQL (`DELETE FROM comparable_adjustments WHERE id = $1` at :632 is a bare primary-key delete). Reachable via `lib.rs:391 .nest("/api/v1/property-valuations", routes::property_valuation::router())` with the aliased mount at :395; router routes at property_valuation.rs:129-133 register GET/POST `/comparables/{comparable_id}/adjustments` and DELETE `/adjustments/{adjustment_id}`. Attack: any authenticated user can `DELETE /api/v1/property-valuations/adjustments/{any_uuid}` to permanently delete adjustments belonging to any other tenant's valuation (adjustments influence the valuation amount — this is both a cross-tenant data destruction AND a valuation-tampering vector), and `POST /api/v1/property-valuations/comparables/{other_org_comparable_uuid}/adjustments` to inject fraudulent adjustments into another org's valuation workflow. Fix shape: load the comparable through an org-scoped repo call (join to valuation → organization_id) and reject when it mismatches `user.tenant_id`, mirroring the pattern used in reserve_funds/vendors (`let org_id = rls.tenant_id(); repo.op(&mut **rls.conn(), org_id, …)`).

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/reports/mod.rs:1540 — `let url = format!("/api/v1/reports/files/{}", file_key);` is returned by `get_execution_download_url` as the only client-facing download link, with `expires_at: now + 1h` implying a presigned URL. But grepping `/api/v1/reports/files` across api-server/src/** finds NO `.route("/files/{...}")` registration anywhere (only `/executions/{id}/download` and `/export/{job_id}/status` exist in the reports router at :238; the file-serving route is not nested elsewhere). The dormancy is acknowledged in a sibling test at tests/suites/report_execution_download_retry_e2e_tests.rs:293-294 ('the actual S3 presigning happens one hop downstream (at the /reports/files/...)') but that downstream hop is not implemented. Reachable from production: `/api/v1/reports/executions/{id}/download` → the response is a dead link that will 404 on every click once the client follows it. Status: this is a re-emit of `code-review-api-handlers-report-dl-deadlink` from signals/2026-07-08-api-handlers.json; verified today (2026-10-14) still present at the same line in the current branch. Fix shape: either (a) register `GET /files/{file_key}` on the reports router that re-authenticates, re-authorizes the caller's org against the file_key's leading org_id, and either streams from S3 (via state.storage_service) or returns a true S3 presigned URL (304); or (b) change get_execution_download_url to return the presigned S3 URL directly from `storage_service.presign_get(&file_key, Duration::hours(1))` and drop the dead intermediate endpoint.
